title: R6B reference case benchmark-options-2-3-6-7: the worked values of options 2 (qualifying affordable housing), 3 (qualifying senior housing), 6 (residences with a community facility) and 7 (a community facility alone) for the benchmark lot (215-16 Northern Boulevard, lot 70 of block 7334, R6B + C2-2, corner), built from two sealed readings per option plus the independent comparer; a value recorded ONLY where both readings agree on the same value and the same basis AND the cited section is captured in docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1; every disagreement, unresolved basis, eligibility and missing fact stays NOT KNOWN; options 5, 8 and 9-10 are named as owed (they rest on uncaptured sections, OUT pending capture task M3-T010); NO rule file, engine, result, capture, register entry, law-library edit or human verdict
objective: Add one new R6B reference case, benchmark-options-2-3-6-7, built from six sealed readings (two per option family: option 2 = provenance -19/-20; option 3 = -21/-22; options 6 and 7 = -23/-24) and the independent comparer (-25), kept unchanged below a short truthful header. Record a value or figure for options 2, 3, 6 and 7 on the benchmark lot (recorded lot area 10,075 sq ft, administrative_record; GIS 10,387.99 display-only, never mixed into a floor-area figure) ONLY where (a) both option readings give it on the same value and the same basis, confirmed by the comparer, AND (b) every cited section is captured in docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1. Rows grouped by option prefix (opt2-*, opt3-*, opt67-*/opt6-*/opt7-*) plus shared rows (both-readers-did-not-have, real-lot-missing-facts, options-out-of-scope). Settled value rows include: opt2 max residential FA 24,180 (2.40 x 10,075, 23-22), UAP affordable FA 4,030 (0.40 x 10,075, 27-111), heights 30/45/65 (23-432), max dwelling units 35 (24,180/680=35.56->35, 23-52(b); matches settled real-lot L7), setback above base 10 wide/15 narrow (23-433); opt3 max residential FA 24,180 (23-22), heights 30/45/65 (23-432), no 23-52 dwelling-unit factor (23-52(a)(2)), AIRS accessory space >= 4% of total floor area (12-10 AIRS), AIRS/LTCF definitions (12-10, eligibility not decided), side yard none/>=5 ft (23-335); opt6/opt7 CF FAR 2.00 and CF max FA 20,150 (24-11 R6B contextual row), combined cap 2.00 greatest single use (24-161, -> 2.40 if residential qualifies), coverage corner 80% / interior 60% (24-11), mixed-level coverage (24-163), heights 30/45/55 (24-04(b)(1)->23-432), CF front yard none (24-34), CF side yard none/>=8 ft (24-35), CF rear yard 30 ft (24-36) with the corner waiver within 100 ft of a <=135-degree corner (24-391), CF rear-yard obstruction (24-33), no FA gain over option 1 (24-162 excepts R6B; 35-33 un-suffixed only), opt7 dwelling units 0, use group III (22-13/32-131). Rows that stay NOT KNOWN: opt3 max dwelling units (23-52 yields no number for a no-factor senior case and no captured provision caps them), opt6 dwelling units (residential/CF split is a design input; bounded at <=29), opt67 street-wall routing (the two readings cite different sections, 23-431 vs 35-631(b); CF-only routing not fixed by captured text), opt67 which CF uses are permitted (22-131..135 uncaptured), opt2 lot coverage / affordable share / MIH-area membership, and the shared real-lot-missing-facts (zoning lot NB-01, lot-area basis NB-04, eligibility). Every quantity names exactly one of the nine measurement bases; no figure mixes bases; no value comes from a program run; nothing is labelled complies/buildable/optimal/feasible; agreement of two AI readings is not proof. Wire the case into the reference-case support (CASE_IDS, REQUIRED_BASE_IDS, the checker, a new step-P9 module with a THIN wiring into check.py, the rendered page) and update the three consumer pins a new case moves.
business_reason: D-094 R007/R075/R084: the full feasibility report owes worked results for all eleven development options; this records four of them, source-backed and independently agreed, as the single source the report/comparison and any later engine take their expected values from (never from program output), and names the other seven as owed so no unavailable option reads as evaluated. R102: the worked values and their per-section capture state feed the zoning-law-library option pages. Options 5, 8 and 9-10 rest on sections not yet in zr-snapshots/v1 and wait for capture task M3-T010; they are out of this task.

risks: RISK 1 (MANDATORY thin wiring, not optional): r6b_reference_cases_check.py is at 591 lines and test_support_files_stay_under_600_lines fails any .py at >= 600. The established step_p7/p8 multi-touchpoint pattern (CASE_READINGS + _READINGS_LABEL + a reading-errors wrapper + must_stay_not_known + quantity_basis + specialised guards) adds ~10 lines and would push check.py to ~601 -> FAIL. step_p9 MUST consolidate all per-row and per-case guards behind ONE entry (e.g. case_errors(case_id,data)) and all reading-digest guards behind ONE entry so check.py grows ~3 lines (1 import + 1 call in validate_case + 1 call in provenance_errors). Do NOT name the step_p9 entry provenance_errors (check.py already defines a top-level provenance_errors) - use a distinct name such as reading_digest_errors wrapped by a step_p9_reading_errors() in check.py. r6b_reference_cases_step_p9.py itself must stay < 600 lines.

RISK 2 (plural 'tables' key): 24-11 and 33-121 carry their FAR/coverage numbers under the plural 'tables' key; the checker's table_assertion reads the singular 'table' (None here) and would fail 'has no table'. Verified: 24-11 R6B contextual row = FAR 2.00, corner 80, interior 60; the prose excerpt only holds the enabling sentence, not the numbers. Record CF FAR 2.00 / coverage 80/60 as arithmetic operands + a verbatim quote of the enabling sentence (present in the excerpt), table_assertion:null; a reviewer eyeballs 2.00/80/60 against the snapshot's R6B contextual 'tables' row. 23-22 and 23-432 (options 2/3) carry singular 'table' -> table_assertion works. 24-161 has no table at all -> quote-only.

RISK 3 (one case, three reading pairs): the generic CASE_READINGS forces one tuple on every row, so the case is NOT registered there; check.py both_readings_errors no-ops for it and step_p9 enforces the pair per row prefix. A negative test MUST prove a one-reading (or wrong-pair) row is refused, or 'both readings agree' is silently unenforced.

RISK 4 (comparer is an adjudicator, not a value source): record only where both option readings agree on the same value and basis; the comparer -25 only confirms agreement and resolves reader-vs-reader disputes (it confirmed every headline number and resolved the Appendix-F capture state, the plural-tables misread and the senior-DU framing). Keep opt3-DU, opt6-DU and opt67-street-wall not_known; never import a single-reader number.

RISK 5 (provenance header honesty): the six reading files and the comparer currently contain NEITHER 'sealed folder' NOR a hard-rule marker (all seven already end END-OF-REPORT). The producer MUST prepend a truthful header to each that supplies the required literal phrase 'sealed folder' and a distinct marker; per the comparer some readers cross-checked the official ZR site, so the header must state the method truthfully and must not claim 'no outside access'. Digests are computed on the saved file AFTER the header is added.

RISK 6 (uncaptured sections): follow the proven convention (zero not_captured citations exist in any current case; both-readers-did-not-have rows name uncaptured sections in prose and cite only captured sections). Record 23-154, 23-63, 74-902/74-903 and 22-131..135 in the prose of not-known / both-readers-did-not-have rows, never as a value basis and never as a formal citation. This also keeps the case within the task's 'only citing sections that are captured' constraint and avoids the forbidden-wording guard.

RISK 7 (scope discipline): options 5, 8 and 9-10 are OUT - their values rest on uncaptured 23-51/23-12/23-371/32-421/33-26/33-301 and wait for capture task M3-T010. The case names them as owed in an options-out-of-scope / real-lot-missing-facts row; recording four options does not narrow the eleven-option scope (R084). Do not edit the law library (R102 is upstream reference only) or any other case file.
RISK 8 (sole reference-case task in flight): must be the only open reference-case task while open; it integrates after M5-T177 and before any further reference-case task.
